sources.title: Sparkles hosted workflow
sources.locator: From prompt to pull request; Which models and agents; security FAQ
sources.finding: Users connect GitHub repositories, choose Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode, submit a prompt and observe cloud work in a browser. The web workflow advertises draft/ready PRs and app-side merge subject to upstream protections. Marketing safety claims are not an independently tested containment result.

sources.title: Sparkles native CLI installation and authentication
sources.locator: Prerequisites; macOS/Linux installer; npm and Windows; Verify installation; Start a session
sources.finding: The CLI runs installed claude, codex or opencode on the local computer. It documents v1.3.0 and a build commit. Each harness retains authentication ownership. Local-only sessions are supported; mirrored sessions require Sparkles login and consent. Platform/channel signing differences are explicit.

sources.title: Sparkles coding-harness selector
sources.locator: Choose the active agent; footer; handoff
sources.finding: The terminal UI selects installed harnesses and restarts into a fresh native local session when switching. Model and reasoning settings are separate. The selector also mentions Grok, but the install/model documentation does not establish its concrete launch/auth route in this bounded pass.

sources.title: Sparkles local model and account boundary
sources.locator: Opening and Why a model may be unavailable
sources.finding: The local harness/provider controls its own authentication, account entitlements and accepted models. Sparkles passes settings to the selected installed runtime; it does not grant provider access. Model names are not extra coding harnesses.

sources.title: Sparkles non-interactive local commands
sources.locator: Select values for one run; configuration precedence
sources.finding: Runtime, model and effort flags also apply to sparkles exec. Repository configuration and environment settings choose defaults while the native harness continues to own credentials. An external CI invocation is not a product-owned scheduler.

sources.title: Sparkles managed sandbox API quickstart
sources.locator: Access grant; create; stream; send follow-up; terminate
sources.finding: Signed-in users create an organization-bound API key, submit repositories and a prompt, then observe an asynchronous managed coding job over authenticated event streams. No API or product was executed during this source pass.

sources.title: Sparkles sandbox lifecycle and PR contract
sources.locator: Access model; Lifecycle; Create requests; Files and pull requests
sources.finding: Sandbox ownership is bound to the exact API access grant, with serialized concurrency checks and lifecycle events. File reads are bounded; agent-driven writes and short-lived repository-scoped GitHub App credentials create or reuse a draft PR. The API contract is narrower than the advertised web draft/ready PR workflow.

sources.title: Sparkles organization credit pricing
sources.finding: The page offers 500 credits for $50 per month, annual billing with twelve months of credits paid for ten, and custom Enterprise deployment on customer infrastructure. One credit corresponds to $0.10 of model inference. Only an initial first-organization grant of 100 credits is advertised; no recurring free cloud allowance is established. The dollar currency code is not stated.

sources.title: Sparkles analytics and replay controls
sources.locator: Section 9, Cookies and Tracking; Privacy settings
sources.finding: The policy says optional PostHog analytics and separately optional masked replay can be rejected, customized or withdrawn through Privacy settings in the app or site footer. Essential authentication/security storage and service logs are separate. The private hosted implementation was not audited.

sources.title: Sparkles hosted service terms
sources.finding: The main service provides coding sandboxes and GitHub PR access under account-based terms. Its design, features and underlying technology belong to Sparkles and are protected intellectual property; customer code remains the customer property. This does not establish the local CLI source license.

sources.title: Sparkles Sandbox API changelog
sources.finding: September 3 adds live working-tree file download. August 6 records organization-bound sandbox operations, event history and scoped limits. These are API component changes, not a dated CLI or full hosted-product release.

sources.title: Sparkles documented CLI channels
sources.finding: The maintainer documentation reports published v1.3.0 installer, Homebrew, npm and GitHub channels, with signing differences and build ead2e9b06711a50b0920cc379f69f8133bb0bc67. The linked GitHub release is inaccessible in the bounded public check, so no release publication timestamp is invented.
